summary: Dortheys Hiyo Eluay International Airport (DJJ) is the primary gateway to Jayapura, the capital of Indonesia's Papua province, located in the town of Sentani on the northern coast of New Guinea. Named after a Papua-born Indonesian military officer and national hero, the airport serves as a critical hub for both domestic and limited international flights in the easternmost region of Indonesia. Its proximity to the scenic Sentani Lake and lush tropical surroundings makes it one of the most picturesque airport approaches in the country.
faqs:
Q: What is Dortheys Hiyo Eluay International Airport named after?
A: The airport is named after Dortheys Hiyo Eluay, an Indonesian Air Force officer and national hero from Papua who was killed in a plane crash in 1993.

Q: Which city does DJJ Airport serve?
A: The airport serves Jayapura, the capital city of Papua province, located about 40 kilometers from the city center.

Q: Are there international flights from DJJ?
A: Yes, the airport handles limited international flights, primarily to neighboring Papua New Guinea, alongside frequent domestic connections to major Indonesian cities like Jakarta, Makassar, and Manado.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport offers standard amenities including dining options, souvenir shops featuring local Papuan crafts, ATMs, and basic passenger lounges, though facilities are more modest compared to larger Indonesian airports.
transport_tips: Taxis and ride-hailing services are the most common ways to reach Jayapura city center, with the journey taking approximately 45 minutes to an hour depending on traffic. Pre-booking a hotel transfer is recommended, as local transport options can be limited, especially for late arrivals. Shared shuttle services and ojek (motorcycle taxis) are also available for shorter trips to nearby Sentani town.
local_tip: If you have a layover or early arrival, visit Sentani Lake just a few kilometers from the airport—the traditional stilt houses and views of the Cyclops Mountains in the background offer a memorable introduction to Papuan culture and landscape.
